subject: The cost figure was measured at rollover -- viability moves from never to about a day, onto timeframes the system already computes
body:
Third version tonight, and this one changes the conclusion rather than adding to it.

I commissioned research on whether intraday FX direction is predictable at all. It came back with
two corrections to things I told you today, and both matter.

CORRECTION ONE. I said the system's direction is a coin flip, based on a 49.6-50.4% hit rate. That
claim was overstated. On 50,000 bars the standard error of a hit rate is 0.22 points, so my
measurement band is plus or minus 0.44. A world-class FX strategy produces a per-bar lift of about
0.05 points -- five times SMALLER than my own measurement noise. My test cannot tell "no signal"
from "excellent signal". The honest version is: no signal big enough to matter at this frequency,
and I could not have seen a normal-sized one anyway.

CORRECTION TWO, and this is the important one. Every cost calculation I did today used a spread of
0.60 ATR, taken from the EA's own startup readings. Those readings were logged at 21:24 and 23:25 --
near rollover, when spreads are at their widest. Estimating the effective spread from price
behaviour instead gives 1.49 pips against the 2.3 quoted, and a median across hours of 0.26 ATR, not
0.60. I had been using a number more than twice the real median, all day.

WHAT THAT DOES TO THE ANSWER.

The required win-rate lift falls with the square root of holding time. The available lift, at the
best annual Sharpe the literature supports for single-pair FX direction, rises with it. Where they
cross is where the system can work.

    5 minutes   short by 142x
    40 minutes  short by 18x
    3 hours     short by 4x     <- the longest horizon I had tested
    1 DAY       VIABLE
    3 days      comfortable
    1 week      comfortable

Under the pessimistic cost figure the crossover moves out to about a week. Either way it EXISTS, and
it is not at three hours. I spent today concluding the system could not work; the corrected
arithmetic says it cannot work AT THIS FREQUENCY, which is a different statement with a different
remedy.

AND THE PART I HAD MISSED ENTIRELY.

The minimum viable hold is roughly 300 to 1,500 five-minute bars. That is the H4 and D1 timeframes
THE SYSTEM ALREADY COMPUTES. The multi-timeframe stack is not wrong about which timeframes carry
information. It uses them to TIME five-minute entries instead of to HOLD multi-day positions. That
is a configuration error rather than a modelling one, and it is the most useful sentence produced
today.

THE HARDER NEWS, so you have both sides.

The specific method family this system is built on has a death certificate in the literature. Neely,
Weller and Ulrich re-tested published FX rules truly out of sample and found moving-average and
filter rules specifically dead by the early 1990s -- not weaker, dead. Marshall and colleagues
tested 7,846 technical rules on five-minute data and found none profitable after correcting for
data snooping. Zero of 7,846. And Zakamulin proves that every moving-average indicator is
algebraically a weighted average of past price changes, so EMA20-versus-EMA50 across five
timeframes is not five votes -- it is five correlated transforms of ONE input. Confluence between
them cannot create information.

That last point independently derives, from first principles, the architectural finding I sent you
earlier: the system has one directional input wearing six coats.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY AVAILABLE ON OUR DATA, per the literature: direction at intraday frequency needs
signed order flow, which OHLC and tick volume cannot supply. What IS both documented and computable
is volatility forecasting and effective-spread estimation. Volatility is the best-forecastable
quantity in high-frequency finance; direction is close to the worst.

NEXT. Add OHLC to the export so the cost ratio can be settled properly rather than through an
unstable proxy, and re-run the specification at a one-day hold instead of four hours, because that
is where the corrected arithmetic says the crossover sits.

37 of 45. Run 5 is still going.
